subject.title: Regression: exec intermittently unavailable in isolated cron sessions (was fixed in 2026.4.1)

question: Should maintainers let the wildcard/profile pull request close this umbrella, or require the remaining scheduler-routing and typed missing-tool status modes to be split or tracked before any closing reference lands?
rationale: The remaining work affects scheduled command execution and cron health semantics, and current open PRs intentionally cover only subsets of the reported behavior.

options.title: Split Before Closing
options.body: Land or reject the wildcard/profile fix on its own merits, but keep this issue open or move the remaining routing/status modes to explicit canonical items before the closing reference can close it.

options.title: Accept Narrow Closure
options.body: Allow the wildcard/profile PR to close this issue and rely on existing adjacent reports for the finite/Codex/status work, accepting that Bug A and Bug C may be harder to find later.

options.title: Hold All Cron Exec Changes
options.body: Pause the open PRs until maintainers choose one unified cron tool-surface and fail-closed policy across wildcard, finite, and Codex paths.

recommendation.title: Split Before Closing
recommendation.body: Land or reject the wildcard/profile fix on its own merits, but keep this issue open or move the remaining routing/status modes to explicit canonical items before the closing reference can close it.

likelyOwner.reason: The unresolved choice is primarily a security-boundary decision around scheduled shell-tool exposure and fail-closed behavior, which matches the related finite-allowlist rationale Josh already commented on.
